subject: Seq2seq
source_sentence: Following Sproat and Jaitly (2016), we implement a seq2seq model trained on window-based data.
title: Neural Text Normalization with Subword Units

subject: Datasets
source_sentence: Our datasets were randomly sampled from a set of 4.9M sentences in the training data portion of the Sproat and Jaitly (2016) data release and split into training, validation, and test data.
title: Neural Text Normalization with Subword Units

subject: Experiments
source_sentence: Our experiments find that an inventory size between 1K and 2K yields the best WER and SER.
title: Neural Text Normalization with Subword Units

subject: Neural Approaches
source_sentence: In this paper, we investigate neural approaches to text normalization which directly translate a written-form sentence to its spoken counterpart without the need of a tagger or grammar.
title: Neural Text Normalization with Subword Units

subject: subwords
source_sentence: We show that the use of subwords can effectively reduce the OOV problem of a baseline seq2seq model with character inputs and token outputs.
title: Neural Text Normalization with Subword Units

subject: Linguistic Features
source_sentence: The addition of linguistic features including casing, word position, POS tags, and edit labels leads to further gains.
title: Neural Text Normalization with Subword Units

subject: Features
source_sentence: We empirically test the addition of each linguistic feature revealing that all features make a contribution to the model, and combining features results in the best performance.
title: Neural Text Normalization with Subword Units

subject: WER
source_sentence: Our model is an improvement over both window-based and sentence-based seq2seq baselines, yielding a WER of 0.17%.
title: Neural Text Normalization with Subword Units
